📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Vogue Business Beauty Tracker, produced in collaboration with Spate, tracks the top five brands, trends and ingredients that are driving the most significant positive change in year-on-year growth that have also demonstrated consistent upward growth historically. Each week, we’ll spotlight a different beauty category and the top five beauty hashtags on TikTok.

Sources indicate that it’s all about the multi-purpose fragrance this week as search data highlights growing interest in fragrances that combine practical formats, occasion-led scents, and distinctive notes. Searches for Chanel’s Coco Mademoiselle Fragrance Primer reflect demand for prep products that extend a scent’s wear, projection, and hold on the skin. Travel fragrance shows continued interest in travel-size versions of full-size scents. Meanwhile, wedding fragrance reflects demand for a dedicated signature scent for the massive day, and white floral perfume highlights interest in scents built around blossoms such as jasmine, gardenia, and tuberose, while pineapple fragrance signals demand for bright, tropical fruit notes.

For fragrance brands, there is growing interest in concept-driven scents, heritage expertise, and affordable fragrance lines. Lore fragrances inspire specific memories, moods, and places, while Toskovat, an independent niche perfume house from Romania, stands out for composing each scent as a “bottled memory”, or extrait de mémoire. Shiseido reflects interest in the Japanese house’s heritage fragrances, with searches focused on Zen. Ranger Station, based in Nashville, draws on music culture and American landscapes for its unisex, artisan-style scents. Finally, Old Navy points to demand for affordable fragrance through Old Navy Beauty Co., its line of hair and body mists, lotions, and body washes, which expanded in August 2026.

It’s all about hair and nail maintenance on TikTok this week.

It has been revealed that #KTipHairExtension reflects interest in semi-permanent extensions, with stylists showing how individual strands are bonded to natural hair using keratin tips. #CurlyHairGel and #CurlyHairVolume highlight interest in curly hair styling, from gels that keep curls defined, hydrated, and frizz-free to techniques that build lift and fullness at the root. #HolidayEyeMakeup points to interest in festive, party-ready eye looks, with tutorials circulating ahead of the winter holidays. Meanwhile, #CuticleRemover centers on at-home nail care, with videos demonstrating how to use Sally Hansen’s Instant Cuticle Remover.

At-home application and retro, graphic designs are among this month’s biggest nail trends. Searches for solid gel polish are on the rise, reflecting demand for a thicker, pot-based gel formula designed for more controlled application, while press-on sets remain popular for their reusability. White chrome powder, which creates a pearly, mirror-like finish when buffed over gel polish, is trending in time for the winter months, as well as geometric nail designs for their clean lines and shapes. Meanwhile, vintage nail polishes, including Urban Decay’s discontinued metallic foil shades, reinforce consumer interest in discontinued products that allow for a nostalgic aesthetic.

For nail brands, DIY manicure solutions, art-driven designs, and everyday nail tools are proving a success. The rise of Cyprus-based brand Doonails reflects demand for do-it-yourself manicure and pedicure products designed to deliver salon-quality results. Never Have I Ever reflects demand for reusable press-on nails featuring licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons, while Double Rhythm underscores interest in accessible soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, and Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

Hair how-to content is ever-growing on TikTok, with creators twisting small sections of coily hair into a #coiltwist or #CurlsWithStraightener tutorials doing the rounds. Meanwhile, the rise in videos showing off #DarkBalayage points to demand for soft, dimensional color finishes on brunette and black hair, which offers a subtle look that minimizes root visibility. There’s also rising demand for lip stains that provide #AllDayLipColor, while #TestingMakeup content demonstrates creators trying out new viral products in their full-face routines, sharing verdicts as they go.

The makeup products consumers are searching for the most are those combining precise application, long wear, and shimmering finishes. Tools such as winged eyeliner stamps take the stress and guesswork out of creating a sharp, even cat-eye look, while creamy lip liners offer buildable definition through soft, blendable formulas. Gripping primers and longwear lipsticks also reflect demand for staying power, from tacky primers that give makeup a sticky base to lip formulas designed to resist fading and transfer. Meanwhile, the rise of rose gold eyeshadow highlights interest in pink-toned metallic shades that add dimension to eye looks.

Sources indicate that when it comes to makeup brands, lasting interest in Burberry Beauty signals the strength of luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses, especially foundations. Nude by Nature highlights demand for makeup powered by natural Australian botanicals. Beauty Creations, a Latina-founded brand, stands out for high-pigment formulas, frequent limited-edition collections, and pop culture partnerships. Sculpted by Aimee, founded by makeup artist Aimee Connolly, reflects interest in multitasking, skin-first products that simplify daily routines. Finally, KeyYou points to demand for lash extension kits and cluster lashes designed for self-application.

Industry observers note that there’s a demand for the nostalgic on TikTok, with the #ThrowBackBeauty hashtag showing creators recreating and reviewing makeup, hair, and fashion looks from past decades. Over on #PerfumeTok, the fragrance community is reviewing, ranking, and recommending scents, while #BlackFridayBeautyDeals points to anticipation ahead of TikTok Shop’s official Black Friday campaign. Meanwhile, #FalseLashesTutorial reflects demand for step-by-step guidance on applying false lashes, and #ServerHairInspo highlights low-maintenance hairstyles built to last throughout the work shift — fueled by the viral “server hair theory” that certain styles can earn servers higher tips.

Skincare products that combine regenerative ingredients, targeted application, and everyday hydration are on the rise in search. Fresh PDRN formats — creams, face masks, and eye patches — reinforce interest in the ingredient, which is associated with cellular repair and a stronger skin barrier, as well as its use in targeted treatments like the Abib PDRN Retinal Eye Patch. Increased searches for hyaluronic acid face lotion reflects demand for deep hydration in everyday skincare, while liquid pimple patches highlight interest in subtle formulas that directly target blemishes and dry into an invisible film.

Skincare consumers are particularly intrigued in brands combining clinical-grade formulas, advanced delivery technologies, and everyday sun protection. Magic Molecule reflects continued demand for hypochlorous acid, offering a multi-purpose, FDA-cleared spray for everyday skincare. KRX Aesthetics and Meditherapy, both South Korean brands, are known for their professional skin treatments adapted for at-home use. Radical Skincare stands out for its performance-driven anti-aging formulas, powered by its proprietary Trylacel delivery technology. Finally, Invisible Zinc reflects demand for mineral-based sunscreens that use zinc oxide as the primary ingredient instead of chemical UV filters.

According to recent reports, over on TikTok, #DolphinSkin reflects interest in ultra-glossy, smooth, and luminous skin, specifically on the body. #GreenChromeNails and #ColorLashes highlight bold approaches to color, from mirror-like metallic manicures in shades of green to multi-colored lash looks. Content featuring #TTSKbeauty, or TikTok Shop K-beauty, shows the platform’s growing role in K-beauty product discovery. Meanwhile, the rise of #JasmineFragrance is driven by Chun Breeze Xian Jasmine, a Chinese fragrance that creators compare to the jasmine tea scent of tea house chains Molly Tea and Heytea.

According to recent reports, in haircare, products that combine scalp support, deep nourishment, and targeted cleansing are trending in search. Peptide hair serums cater to those seeking lightweight formulas that support fuller-looking hair, with searches associated primarily with The Ordinary’s Multi-Peptide Serum for Hair Density, while hair thinning serums points to a broader focus on density and scalpcare. Rice water hair spray highlights interest in a convenient leave-in format for an ingredient valued for adding strength and shine. Cholesterol hair treatment reflects demand for rich, deep-conditioning masks that restore moisture and softness, and chlorine removal shampoo signals demand for clarifying formulas that remove chlorine build-up post-swim.

In a recent development, when it comes to brands, the rise of K-beauty player Lilyeve reflects demand for daily scalpcare, with searches led by its Scalp Turn Cica PDRN Brush Ampoule, a cooling leave-in treatment applied through a built-in brush head. Demand for Honeyque products highlights interest in salon-grade Japanese haircare designed to repair dry, damaged and frizzy hair, while Chāmpo stands out for blending ayurvedic principles with modern trichology, particularly through its hair serum. Bare Anatomy underscores continued demand for science-backed, dermatologically tested haircare, from anti-dandruff shampoo to a roll-on scalp serum. Finally, Brickell Men’s Products reflects interest in natural grooming formulated specifically for men.

It has been revealed that beyond traditional beauty content, #MakeupGame on TikTok reflects the growing overlap between beauty and gaming, with posts centered around Makeup Mania, a Roblox game where players compete through makeup and fashion looks. #HowToSilkPress and #4CWashDay highlight continued demand for textured hair education, from step-by-step silk press tutorials to wash day routines tailored to tightly coiled 4C hair. The #GlitterAcrylic hashtag points to interest in sparkling, statement acrylic nail sets, while #EczemaPatch shows the hydrocolloid format popularized by pimple patches expanding to eczema-prone skin.

Industry observers note that in the wellness world, there’s growing interest in specialized nutrition and brands that prioritize convenience and targeted health benefits. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, high-protein formats, with ready-to-drink shots providing 23 grams of protein per serving. Sisel highlights a broad approach to wellness through dietary supplements and functional beverages, while Toplux Nutrition emphasizes science-backed supplements at affordable prices. Wip stands out for its nicotine-free caffeine pouches, offering a convenient format for an energy boost. Finally, Triquetra Health reflects interest in gut and metabolic wellness, with searches focused on its GLP-Pro probiotic and postbiotic supplement. Collectively, these brands span everyday protein intake, energy support, and targeted nutritional supplementation.

In the midst of October, #HalloweenHairClips are trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in festive, spooky hair accessories — particularly horror-themed claw clips and seasonal designs. Meanwhile, the rise of #LadybugMakeup highlights whimsical, insect-inspired makeup looks also tailored to spooky season. Across manicure content, #UglyNails are performing well, as more unconventional and unusual nail designs gain traction for allowing artistic expression, while #PinkCateyeNails reflects interest in light-reflecting cateye designs in shades of pink. The #CoilyCurly hashtag celebrates natural hair textures between curly and coily, with content focused on haircare tips and styling.

It has been revealed that products that combine hydration, targeted care and sensory experiences are ruling the bodycare category. Hydrating body mists meet demand for lightweight, water-like moisturizers that deliver lotion-level hydration, while anti-sweat hand creams offer targeted solutions for managing perspiration on the hands. Growing demand for hand mists suggest interest in convenient, fragrant formats that refresh and sanitize on the go, while niacinamide body wash is an example of products designed to support the skin’s moisture barrier. Finally, strawberry body scrub reflects demand for fruit-inspired bodycare that combines exfoliation with appealing scents and ingredients.

Across bodycare brands, there’s growing interest in those offering specialized and efficient approaches to personal care and grooming. Carpe reflects demand for clinical-strength sweat and odor control, while Hanni highlights simplified bodycare through “skip-step” essentials, with a particular rise in searches for its Splash Salve in-shower body balm. Proraso stands out for its Italian men’s grooming heritage. Estée Lauder has evolved its fragrance range by incorporating bodycare into its iconic scent collections, as searches for its Beautiful Perfumed Body Powder grow. Meanwhile, Prequel reflects interest in dermatologist-developed, science-backed skincare centered on skin barrier health.

In a recent development, this week on TikTok, the #DiscountMakeup hashtag is flooded with shoppers unexpectedly discovering Jeffree Star Cosmetics products at Dollar Tree. Meanwhile, content around #PerfumeMists is focused on reviews and recommendations of lightweight, refreshing fragrance formats. #TattooLipLiner content is also on the rise, featuring ink-like liners, peel-off stains, and semi-permanent lip treatments for long-lasting lip definition. #GlowyMakeupRoutine points to interest in luminous, radiant makeup looks and routines, while #FeatheredHair highlights interest in the ’70s voluminous, heavily layered hair look. Together, these trends highlight how beauty content is increasingly shaped by product discovery, makeup routines and nostalgic aesthetics.

Sources indicate that there’s growing interest in fragrance trends that combine personalization, identity, and convenience. Alcohol-free fragrances, for example, reflect demand for alternative formulations to traditional perfumes, while custom perfumes point to interest in personalized scents tailored to individual preferences. The rise of masculine fragrances suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male and female consumers alike, while gothic perfume reflects demand for darker and more mysterious aromatic profiles that evoke the romantic and atmospheric elements of the goth aesthetic. Finally, travel fragrances, the portable and convenient scent formats designed to make fragrance easier to pack and use on the go, are also trending.

In a recent development, this month, there’s particular interest in fragrance brands offering distinctive approaches to scent. Lore’s emotive, transportive fragrances translate specific moods and places into immersive scent experiences, while MCM Fragrance and Miu Miu highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend recognizable fashion identities into fragrance, with searches for the latter mainly associated with Miutine and its youthful fragrance identity. Ranger Station stands out for its bold, high-concentration, nature-inspired scents, while Maison d’Etto offers perfumes rooted in equestrian influence, contemporary art and architecture. These brands highlight growing consumer interest in fragrance that goes beyond scent itself, offering distinctive stories, identities and sensory experiences.

Sources indicate that as we enter October season, #SpookyNailArt is trending on TikTok, reflecting interest in Halloween-inspired nail designs based on playful motifs. Meanwhile, growing interest in the #MakeupColorTheory reinforces the rise of consumers learning about the hues that enhance their features. #ConcertHair highlights demand for hairstyles that are durable, creative and highly accessorized, specifically designed to last throughout a concert, while the #RomanticUpdo reflects interest in soft, feminine hairstyles and intentionally undone styles. #CologneHaul shows interest in discovering and showcasing fragrance purchases and collections.

When it comes to nails, there’s a growing interest in trends that combine precision, personalization, and visually distinct finishes. The Italian manicure, which creates the appearance of longer slender nails, reflects demand for more precise techniques, while nail art pens and letters on nails point to interest in customized designs and intricate details. The rise of glass nail polish highlights a preference for glossy, translucent finishes, and vibrant nails reflect demand for bold, eye-catching colors.

Recent findings suggest that among this month’s trending nail brands, there’s a clear preference for distinct approaches to at-home manicures. Reusable, press-on nail line Never Have I Ever incorporates licensed artwork from independent artists and cultural icons into nail designs, while Double Rhythm reinforces interest in accessible, soak-off gel polishes and nail art supplies for DIY and salon-style looks. IPolish stands out for its digital color-changing press-on nails, allowing consumers to switch between hundreds of shades using a smartphone and activation wand. Heyhae offers sun-cured gel nail strips that harden naturally in sunlight without requiring a traditional UV or LED lamp, while Sparkle & Co. specializes in DIY dip powders with unique glitters, foils, flakes, glow-in-the-dark, and color-changing effects.

Industry observers note that tikTok is seeing an influx of content featuring #BumperBangs, reflecting interest in vintage 1940s and ’50s fringe styles consisting of a bold, rounded shape. Meanwhile, the rise of #CurlyHairBride highlights demand for bridal hair inspiration that embraces natural curls and textured styles. #WigsOnTikTok reveals the growing role of TikTok in discovering, styling, and showcasing wigs. #UltaFragrance and #SephoraBeautyAdvisor highlight interest in beauty advisors sharing recommendations, product expertise and customer interactions at retailers Ulta and Sephora. Together, these hashtags highlight interest in vintage looks, occasion-specific styling, and behind-the-scenes beauty retail experiences.

In a recent development, there’s a growing interest in makeup products that combine ease of use, enhanced appearance, and convenient beauty benefits, according to monthly search data. Growth in creamy lip liners points to demand for smooth, easy-to-apply products that shape and define the lips, while lip volumizers help create the appearance of fuller, smoother lips without invasive treatments. Rose gold eyeshadow is also trending, driven by demand for warm, luminous shades. Gripping primer, which is a gel-based product with a tacky finish to hold your makeup in place, reflects interest in creating durable makeup looks that last throughout the day. The rise of SPF face powder reveals interest in facial sun protection beyond conventional sunscreens, with multifunctional products that both protect and control shine.

Recent findings suggest that across makeup brands, those offering distinctive products spanning various price points are performing particularly well. Hung Vanngo Beauty reflects demand for makeup artist expertise, while Burberry Beauty signals continued interest in luxury cosmetics from established fashion houses. C-beauty brand Cheeryep and Sleek Makeup highlight demand for vibrant, high-pigment makeup and innovative finishes. Maven Beauty, Fashion Nova’s makeup brand, suggests growing demand for affordable beauty options.

On TikTok, #UVHairExtensions are gaining traction, reflecting interest in innovative UV and LED hair extension techniques offering fast application, while #BrownRedHair highlights demand for rich, warm hair color combinations of brown, red, copper, and mahogany tones. Manicurist content featuring #PracticeNails shows past designs and their training progress, while #CottagecoreNails spotlights whimsical, nature-inspired manicures influenced by cottagecore aesthetics. The rise of #BridesmaidsMakeup reflects growing demand for beauty inspiration tailored to bridesmaids and wedding looks.

In skincare, monthly interest in products and treatments that combine targeted skin health benefits with gentle, barrier-supporting ingredients and advanced technologies is rising. Silicone-free sunscreen and its lightweight, ingredient-conscious sun protection is trending, while the retinol sandwich method, where retinol is layered between moisturizer to reduce the risk of irritation, is gaining traction among those looking to safely introduce retinol into their routines. There is continued demand for hyaluronic acid face lotions offering convenient, hydrating properties that support moisture retention and skin plumpness, while ceramide toners are designed to strengthen and maintain the skin barrier. Interest in high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) treatments highlights demand for advanced, non-invasive aesthetic treatments focused on skin tightening and rejuvenation.

For brands, those offering science-backed and targeted skincare solutions are trending. Elm Biosciences, which develops clinical skincare focused on healthy aging and cellular-level care, is gaining traction, while Magic Molecule offers hypochlorous acid solutions that cleanse, reduce inflammation and support skin healing. The rise of TropicSport signals demand for high-performance sun protection during active lifestyles. NewGel+ reflects interest in specialized scarcare and skin repair. The Body Shop, particularly its Drops of Youth line, highlights demand for products targeting early signs of aging while supporting skin resilience against daily environmental stressors.

According to recent reports, on TikTok, #SheinMakeupHaul is trending, reflective of the growing interest in discovering and sharing affordable makeup products through beauty hauls. #BestHairOils demonstrates how more consumers are comparing different hair oils and seeking product recommendations. #BakedBlush features content spotlighting new blush launches and shades comparisons through product swatches and reviews. #TinselBraids and #CakeNails highlight playful approaches to self-expression through decorative hairstyles and creative nail designs, with consumers exploring visually distinctive looks.

It has been revealed that this month’s search data highlights growing interest in haircare products that combine targeted follicle growth with plant-based ingredients. Popular hair serums range from including specific active ingredients, with searches for redensyl and peptide serums that help reduce shedding by supporting follicle health and improving fullness, to concern-specific searches such as hair thinning serum. Rice water hairspray highlights demand for convenient, multifunctional products that can strengthen strands, add shine and reduce frizz, while plant-based shampoos reflect growing interest in products made primarily with vegan and botanical ingredients.

When it comes to haircare brands, those offering performance-driven, science-backed and premium solutions, in particular, are trending. Labo-H reflects demand for Korean scalpcare and hair loss prevention, while UltraSwim highlights interest in cleansing products designed to remove chlorine, chemical odors, and mineral buildup from hair. Bare Anatomy signals demand for science-backed haircare, addressing specific concerns such as shedding, dandruff, frizz, and damage, while Bvlgari Beauty reflects interest in luxury products combining cleansing and scalpcare with the brand’s signature scents. Meanwhile, Iso Beauty highlights growing interest in solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home.

Over on TikTok, #BabyShowerMakeup reflects interest in soft glam makeup looks tailored specifically for mothers and guests attending baby showers, while #MarchMakeup demonstrates makeup looks based on the birthday month. #QuickCurls highlights demand for fast and easy hairstyling techniques for curly hair, while #LakeHair reflects interest in solutions to avoid or untangle the messy, textured, and sometimes dry or mineral-coated hair associated with freshwater swimming. #AntioxidantSerum shows dermatologist content discussing skincare products centered around antioxidant benefits and protection from environmental stressors.

Across wellness, monthly search data highlights growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits, convenience, and ease of use. Dopamine patches, for example, reflect demand for wearable solutions associated with mood and focus support, while acupressure wristbands reveal interest in convenient solutions for managing and preventing nausea, particularly concerning travel and motion sickness. Screenless fitness trackers demonstrate growing demand for minimalist wearable technology that passively monitors health and activity data without the distraction of a screen. Men’s fertility supplements signal interest in targeted nutritional support for male reproductive health, while liquid zinc supplements highlight demand for convenient ways to prevent or address zinc deficiency and support immune health.

For brands, there’s growing interest in those offering targeted, convenient, and science-backed wellness solutions. Pure Genius Protein reflects demand for portable, easy-to-consume protein products, while Artemis Tea highlights interest in organic herbal teas and wellness blends rooted in traditional herbalism. Nancy’s Probiotic signals demand for organic cultured foods and probiotic-focused nutrition, while EFX Sports reflects interest in performance supplements such as Kre-Alkalyn creatine, designed to support strength and recovery. The rise of Sparkle Wellness relates to continued interest in collagen supplements targeting skin, hair, nails, and overall vitality.

Industry observers note that over on TikTok, the growing traction for #BridalUpdoStyle reflects interest in polished, occasion-ready hairstyles for weddings and special events. #FauxBrows and #HowToSelfTan highlight different approaches to enhancing everyday beauty, from creating realistic, hair-like brow strokes to achieving an even, natural-looking tan at home. #MakeupPR reflects the influencer culture around receiving and unboxing gifted beauty products, as well as creators sharing their experiences with brands. #MakeupOver35 highlights growing interest in makeup techniques and product recommendations tailored to women over the age of 35.

It has been revealed that in the bodycare space, current search trends highlight growing interest in products that combine targeted benefits and convenience with sensory appeal. Alpha hydroxy (AHA) body lotions and hand exfoliators reflect demand for exfoliating and smoothing products that help remove dead skin cells, dirt, and dry patches. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetics. Epsom salt lotions reflect interest in convenient options for muscle relief and recovery, while kojic acid lotions signal demand for targeted brightening and uneven skin tone care.

In a recent development, as for bodycare brands, those offering targeted, skin-friendly solutions are gaining traction. QV Skincare reflects demand for sensitive skin and barrier-supportive care, while Naked Bee highlights interest in affordable, natural bodycare options incorporating ingredients such as honey, beeswax, and oatmeal. Derman points to demand for targeted antifungal treatments, and Curology reflects growing interest in dermatologist-designed solutions for body breakouts and rough texture. Meanwhile, Luna Daily highlights demand for pH-balanced, microbiome-friendly care for both the body and intimate areas. These brands reveal how the category is evolving through specialist treatments based on body area and skin concern, spanning natural-based products to dermatologist-designed solutions.

Recent findings suggest that over on TikTok, #VampNails reflect interest in bold, dramatic nail looks inspired by dark and vampy aesthetics. #RootRetouch and #GrayGrowOut highlight different approaches to managing hair color, from concealing visible roots to embracing the transition to natural gray. #HairVolumeHacks signals demand for accessible styling techniques that create fuller, more voluminous hair. #MakeupTrial reflects interest in testing and refining makeup looks ahead of weddings and special events.

This month’s search data highlights a shift toward more occasion-driven and emotionally evocative fragrance choices. The rise of wedding fragrances reflects growing interest in scents associated with meaningful celebrations and special occasions. Sport fragrances signal demand for fresh, energetic scents suited to active lifestyles and everyday wear, while sweet fragrances highlight continued preference for gourmand and indulgent scent profiles, with birthday cake perfume, for example, also offering a familiar scent evocative of childhood memories. Electric perfume, meanwhile, with searches mainly associated with the iconic Revlon fragrance from the 80s, Electric Youth, reflects the enduring appeal of discontinued scents that offer a upcoming form of nostalgia.

According to recent reports, when it comes to brands, DefineMe Creative Studio highlights growing interest in fragrance rooted in pop culture, with collaborations such as Barbie connecting scent with recognizable characters and cultural identities. Lore reflects demand for emotive, transportive fragrances that translate specific moods and places into scent experiences. Miu Miu and MCM Fragrance highlight growing interest in luxury scents that extend a recognizable fashion identity into the perfume space, with Miu Miu searches mainly associated with the more youthful and feminine Miutine scent. The rise of Kopari, specifically its fragrance mists, reflects demand for lighter fragrance formats suited to everyday use.

On TikTok, #CreamEyeshadowSticks are trending, as demand rises for convenient, easy-to-apply makeup formats that allow consumers to create smooth, buildable eye looks with minimal effort. #ChunkyHighlights and #NailFoils reflect growing interest in creative beauty techniques that add dimension and visual impact to hair and nails. #UltaHairSalon reflects consumers’ and salon workers’ experiences with hair services in retail stores, highlighting a convenient way to access professional salon expertise. The continued interest in #DrySkinSolutions signals demand for targeted skincare solutions focused on relieving dryness and supporting skin hydration.

There’s been a rise in search data for nail art pens, reflecting growing interest in personalized nail creativity that’s nostalgic and enables consumers to experiment with intricate and customized designs. Liquid tape reflects demand for manicure tools that simplify application while improving precision and creating cleaner, more professional-looking results. Glitter nail polish is another Y2K trend regaining momentum, with continued interest in bold, statement-making finishes that add a dose of playfulness to nail looks. The sustained demand for glass nail polish underscores the role of high-gloss translucent finishes as a more classic aesthetic. Meanwhile, celestial nails signal increasing enthusiasm for imaginative and artistic nail designs inspired by cosmic themes and metallic accents.

Sources indicate that nars, which phased out its nail polish line, is trending in search data, reflecting the enduring appeal of discontinued beauty products when consumers maintain connections with iconic shades and search for color dupes still available on the market. Tonic Polish and Pure Ice, meanwhile, highlight growing interest in expressive nail finishes, such as multichromes, magnetics and holographics, as well as accessible trend-driven shades, glitters and metallics that keep manicures more unique. Beyond polish, Burt’s Bees highlights growing demand for nourishing nailcare solutions, such as cuticle creams that provide hydration while supporting dry and brittle nails. Diamond Cosmetics signals continued interest in accessible nail products that offer variety and affordability.

On TikTok, #BrighteningEyeMasks reflect demand for targeted skincare solutions, with consumers using under-eye patches to depuff, hydrate, and reduce the appearance of dark circles. Content featuring #MakeupDisaster and #BadNailsCheck highlights the interest from consumers in beauty mishaps, from makeup products that fail to deliver expected results to manicure disasters and negative salon experiences. #SkincareRitual reflects interest in consistent, personalized skincare routines focused on daily maintenance. #NailTechDayInMyLife reflects interest in behind-the-scenes nail content, with consumers engaging with nail technicians’ routines, creative processes, and the realities of running a nail business. Together, these trends reflect growing consumer interest in authentic beauty experiences and personal routines.

In the makeup space, monthly data highlights growing demand for innovative, personalized, and tech-driven cosmetics. In the haircare space, there is growing interest in haircare solutions that combine convenience and science-backed ingredients alongside targeted treatments to support hair and scalp health. On TikTok, #BadNailsCheck has users showing manicure disasters, sharing nail art that turned out completely different from the reference photo. In the wellness space, there’s a growing interest in supplements and solutions that support long-term health, targeted nutrition, and proactive selfcare. On TikTok, the #SummerGlowMakeup and #BeautyFavs hashtags reflect growing interest in curated beauty routines and product discovery, with consumers seeking seasonal makeup inspiration alongside trusted product recommendations. #GeodeNails lean into a demand for artistic, statement-making nail designs that emphasize creativity and self-expression. #DIYMicroLocsJourney adopts a personal storytelling format, as consumers document their hair journeys, while learning protective hair styling techniques. In the bodycare category, there’s growing interest in products that combine targeted treatments, ingredient-focused formulations, and at-home wellness solutions. Industry observers note that over on TikTok, #CheetahHair, #HaircutTutorials, and #HairFoils are all trending, reflecting a broader shift toward more experimental and technique-driven approaches to hair styling. #CheetahHair highlights bold, pattern-led hair looks that emphasize self-expression and visual impact, #HaircutTutorials points to the growing demand for accessible, step-by-step education from hair stylists, while #HairFoils underscores continued interest in professional coloring techniques. Luxury fragrances are becoming more than a special occasion spritz. Consumers are investing in scents that have wide appeal, from sport fragrances for energy, freshness, and an active lifestyle, to sweet smells that have a touch of nostalgia.

Tomato perfume underscores the rise of unconventional fragrance notes, reflecting curiosity around earthy and garden-fresh scent experiences that stand apart from traditional or gourmand offerings. #RedDyedHair, #LashDye, and #SelfTannerHack all reflect a broader shift toward at-home beauty experimentation through DIY techniques. #RedDyedHair highlights bold self-applied color changes as a form of personal expression and transformation. #LashDye reflects interest in low-maintenance beauty routines, where users tint lashes for longer-lasting definition, and #SelfTannerHack shows how shared tips are used to achieve more controlled, even tanning results. Then, #NosePatches and #NeckSkincareRoutine point to growing demand for targeted skincare solutions, with the former focusing on pore care and blackheads for a quick, temporary smoothing effect, while the latter underscores increasing awareness of often-neglected areas that require attention beyond the face. Together, these trends reflect a move into DIY-driven beauty and targeted treatment routines.

When it comes to nails, consumers are seeking designs that blend self-expression, practicality, and care. BB cream nails reflect demand for natural-looking, low-maintenance manicures, while comic nails highlight a desire for creative and expressive nail art. Matcha nails point to the growing traction of soft green tones, influenced by the cult popularity of the beverage, while solid gel nail glue indicates interest in durable, mess-free nail application, as consumers increasingly value long-lasting performance. The rise of The Gelbottle, Nail Reformation, Kleo Kolor, and Curvlife each proves growing demand for long-lasting nail solutions that deliver salon-quality results. The Gelbottle reflects interest in professional-grade systems that strengthen and enhance natural nails, while Nail Reformation and Kleo Kolor point to the popularity of reusable press-ons and durable at-home manicure options. Recent findings suggest that on TikTok, #CyberPunkNails reflects interest in futuristic nail art that combines punk influences, neon accents, metallic finishes, and bold 3D details. #SkinTintStick highlights demand for hybrid complexion products that offer light coverage with skincare benefits in a portable format. #TCAPeel and #MicrobiomeSkincare signal growing consumer interest in understanding the mechanisms behind skin behavior, from chemical exfoliation and skin renewal to the role of the microbiome in barrier health. In the case of #TCAPeel, viral social media content often emphasizes the risks of extreme at-home use. #HairLossJourney extends this same behavior pattern into haircare, where individuals actively seek to understand the causes of hair loss, sharing progress and seeking support and solutions. According to recent reports, makeup products and techniques that deliver precision, convenience, and natural-looking results are soaring. Meanwhile, cool-toned blush and cool-toned contour underscore consumers’ increasing focus on shade accuracy. At the same time, ghost and pre-glued lashes highlight demand for effortless lash enhancement, combining natural-looking results with faster and easier application methods. In a recent development, across makeup brands, the rise of Elroel and Purito highlights the continued influence of K-beauty. Dermatologist-founded Rodan and Fields further reinforces interest in hybrid complexion products that combine cosmetic performance with skincare benefits. As more consumers focus on maintaining hair health and reducing damage, #BedtimeHaircare is trending on TikTok and reflects growing interest in overnight prevention treatments. #CollagenFilm highlights K-beauty innovation in the form of dissolvable collagen films, designed for topical application to deliver instant hydration and a smoother, firmer appearance. #BrowFreeze, meanwhile, reflects continued interest in lifted, feathered brow styling that creates a laminated look. #613AmazonWig signals demand for affordable, pre-lightened platinum blonde wigs that enable bold color experimentation without chemical processing, while #GluelessClosureInstall reflects a broader shift in wig culture toward accessible, low-damage styling, where consumers seek dramatic transformations that are easy to apply, comfortable to wear, and avoid the long-term commitment or potential damage associated with traditional installation methods. Recent findings suggest that consumers are on the hunt for science-led skincare innovations. Among trending skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores the rise in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Wow Skin Science reflects demand for nature-inspired skincare, offering plant-powered formulations free from harsh chemicals. According to recent reports, consumers are increasingly drawn to wellness formats that blend supplementation, wearables, and at-home recovery tools into everyday routines. GLP-1 and NAD+ patches support metabolism, energy, and cellular function, and multi-collagen supplements continue to gain traction for beauty and structural benefits such as skin, hair, and joint health. According to recent reports, consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara highlights how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

In a recent development, the top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Maange highlights that consumers are investing in quality makeup brushes and application tools, signaling increased interest in the techniques behind the look, not just the formulas themselves. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

The rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids highlights that consumers are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

In a recent development, skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. Also, melting lip balms and pore care are trending as consumers seek results‑driven everyday products.

Sources indicate that brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as users experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

Industry observers note that exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

Sources indicate that kate McLeod and Brown Sugar Babe offer sensory bodycare experiences, from exfoliating stones to whipped butters. Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Bend Soap Company’s artisanal approach highlights the appeal of small‑batch, craft formulations.

According to recent reports, these top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. The popularity of #ScienceBasedSkincare and #SkincareApp indicates that users are increasingly seeking data‑informed products and digital tools. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. On the makeup side, #BlushLovers highlights the enduring appeal of color cosmetics.

The surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

Matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. La Sultane de Saba Paris channels consumer interest with olfactory-inspired notes. Similarly, The Maker Perfume hints at a growing demand for identity‑driven scent choices over mass market fragrances. Meanwhile, legacy and designer‑adjacent brands like Hugo Boss and Penhaligon’s continue to draw attention for their heritage and status, even as they explore niche alternatives.

Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

Recent findings suggest that the popularity of #SensitiveSkincare demonstrates more people are seeking gentle, irritation‑free formulas. Meanwhile, #UnderratedSkincare suggests a hunger for hidden gems or under-the-radar products, meaning consumers are increasingly willing to explore beyond mainstream brands. The rise of #BlondeHighlightsOnDarkHair and #HairLoss captures demand for hair‑specific solutions and transformation content, as customers look for guidance and community advice on challenging hair goals. Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

In a recent development, bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. The appetite for animalistic styles continues with cat eye nails reflecting excitement around method‑driven finishes — using magnetic polish to create shimmering dimension that feels both futuristic and accessible. Water drop nails and junk nails are also making noise with sleek, sculptural texture for the former and a maximalist approach to the latter with oversized charms, clashing textures and extreme customization.

Consumers are leaning into at-home expertise and expressive finishes. Gaoy and MelodySusie highlight a growing investment in DIY tools like gel kits, lamps and drills. Nail Labo caters to a rising demand for precision and minimalist artistry, drawing from Japanese nail culture that prioritizes clean lines, quality materials and technical skill. Caudalie introduces a skincare-forward angle with its hand and nailcare rooted in antioxidant-rich formulations. Meanwhile, Ethereal Lacquer is capturing attention through its holographic, metallic and multi-chrome polishes, signaling that many nail consumers are seeking and collecting bold, light-catching finishes that double as artistic self-expression.

According to recent reports, the popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where consumers seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Lastly, #EdgeControlFor4cHair emphasizes the demand for texture-specific solutions and culturally resonant beauty techniques.

Matte powder is trending, as consumers seek polished, smooth and filtered‑like skin finishes. The popularity of pink lip stain and lipstick pencil, meanwhile, highlights a tilt toward bold lip looks that are still accessible and day‑to‑day friendly. Techniques like tightline eyeliner illustrate how subtle definition is gaining traction, reflecting a preference for minimal effort with big impact. Contrastingly, the surge in black lip stains suggest that consumers are also embracing more daring, identity‑driven looks that go beyond enhancement.

According to recent reports, among the top‑growing makeup brands, there’s an emphasis on accessible, niche aesthetics and cultural authenticity across price points. BBIA’s K‑beauty roots and affordable, vibrant product lines show how makeup lovers are drawn to colorful products that promote self-expression. Kulfi Beauty’s South Asian-inspired, inclusive shade range underscores a demand for brands that acknowledge and celebrate underrepresented skin tones and identities. On the other end of the pricing spectrum, Hermès brings luxury craftsmanship and premium finishes to makeup, signaling that consumers also view beauty as a status and lifestyle experience. Meanwhile, Palladio Beauty and UCoolMe illustrate how ingredient-driven products and purpose‑driven formats (like lash clusters) are becoming non‑negotiable for many buyers.

Industry observers note that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer behavior shift toward accessibility, self‑expression and targeted problem‑solving. The surge in #EyelashLiftAndTint showcases how users are seeking out tutorial‑friendly content and at‑home techniques to achieve salon‑level transformations. Meanwhile, #BraidingExtensions and #NailsDesignIdeas point to a growing appetite for creative styling and personalization in hair and nails. At the same time, #KojicAndTurmericSoap highlights the fascination with viral, ingredient‑centric skincare that promises visible pay-off through ‘miracle’ formulas. Lastly, #PinkLipLiner reflects a subtle shift from cool-tone nudes toward warmer, reddish-pink tones that add soft color while still feeling natural — indicating consumers’ evolving preference for makeup that enhances without overpowering.

The rise of morning shed, the ritualized removal of multiple overnight beauty tools and treatments, highlights a growing fascination with stacked, intensive skincare routines that promise overnight results. Searches for face-lifting masks reflect a desire for visible tightening, while hydrogel’s jelly-like, cooling texture satisfies a craving for sensorial, soothing formats. Meanwhile, rising interest in milky toners and turmeric face creams reveals demand for gentle nourishment and targeted actives, with turmeric specifically valued for its natural, hyperpigmentation-reducing benefits.

By brand, Grace & Stella and Byoma each represent a demand for approachable, feel-good skincare — whether through playful formats like eye masks or barrier-repair formulas that emphasize maintenance and simplicity. In contrast, brands like AnteAge, Bioeffect and Medik8 cater to a results-focused audience seeking science-led actives like EGF and retinal, signaling rising trust in clinical, regenerative skincare that targets aging and skin renewal at a deeper level. Consumers are embracing a dual approach to skincare, blending routine-friendly support with targeted, high-performance treatments, depending on need, mood, or life stage.

According to recent reports, in the TikTok sphere, trending beauty hashtags are focusing on age inclusivity, professional-level prep, and tailored care for specific identities and beauty concerns. #BeautyOver60 spotlights content that speaks directly to mature audiences, as those aged 60-plus seek routines and products that speak to their evolving needs and celebrate aging confidently. #BridalSkinPrep, often used by makeup artists, reflects interest in expert-driven techniques that enhance makeup application, as consumers value the behind-the-scenes steps that create flawless, event-ready skin. Meanwhile, #CollegeHairstylist, #RedHaircare and #CeramideSerum point to highly specialized content — from on-campus hairstyling services to color-specific hair routines and barrier-supporting ingredients — illustrating a broader trend toward community-rooted expertise and ingredient-conscious skincare.

It has been revealed that haircare is of increasing importance to consumers, as beauty focuses go beyond the surface to tackle cosmetic concerns at their root. The rise of DHT blocker shampoos and scalp serums signal growing concern around hair thinning and scalp health, with consumers turning to targeted treatments that address hair loss at its source. Interest in lightweight conditioners and hair UV protection highlights desire for gentle hydration and environmental defense, which avoids build-up and leans into skincare. Hair fiber powders are also rising, especially among young males, as consumers seek quick-fix solutions to thinning and receding, challenges becoming more prevalent in social dialogue.

Industry observers note that among haircare brands, there’s a consumer shift toward precision and wellness‑infused formulations. Cerave’s expansion into haircare underscores the demand for dermatologist‑approved, barrier‑support solutions — with ceramides and niacinamide anchoring formulas that consider scalp health as closely tied to hair health. Arey taps into a preventative and repigmentation‑focused niche by offering clinical systems to address greying hair, as more consumers seek anti‑aging hair solutions. Design Essentials and TGIN highlight a growing emphasis on texture‑specific haircare, delivering salon‑quality formulas for relaxed, natural and coily hair types. Meanwhile, Vichy brings its skin‑science heritage to hair with targeted treatments for dandruff.

Recent findings suggest that on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer shift toward efficiency, targeted solutions and hacks. The rise of #OnTheGoMakeup highlights how beauty routines are being compressed and adapted for busy lifestyles. #ChopstickCurls, referring to tight, defined curls achieved with ultra-thin rectangular-shaped wands, reflects consumer interest in niche, high-impact styling tools. Hashtags like #DepuffSkin, #OilySkinSolutions and #MicellarWaterHacks point to a demand for quick‑acting, problem‑solving formulas, especially those that tackle puffiness, oil control, or simplify skincare cleansing — reflecting an audience that wants visible change with minimal fuss.

In a recent development, in the evergrowing wellness space, consumers are leaning into metabolic health, enhanced performance and functional supplementation. As the links between gut health and other bodily concerns continue to emerge, consumers are turning to natural tools for internal balance and immunity support. Ketone and NAD supplements reveal that biohacking and longevity are still on consumers’ minds, as they seek ways to improve energy, cellular repair and cognitive performance through next-gen supplementation. When it comes to wellness brands, Puori stands out for its ultra‑transparent, minimalist supplements that indicate a strong consumer demand for trustworthy quality and ingredient purity. Javy Coffee merges convenience and function by offering high‑protein, sugar‑free coffee concentrates, hinting that wellness is being woven into everyday routines as well as indulgent moments. Lastly, Snap Supplements and Alaya Naturals emphasize science‑backed formulas, superfood blends and adaptogens, while highlighting how modern consumers are gravitating toward preventative, system‑focused wellness — gut, hormones, vitality — rather than generic multivitamins.

It has been revealed that fragrance notes like tonka bean, marshmallow and chocolate are doing the rounds this month, marking a shift towards gourmand scents that evoke warmth, nostalgia and emotional selfcare. Recent findings suggest that tikTok’s trending beauty hashtags reflect a consumer focus on practicality, preparedness and style-conscious experimentation. #SkincareWithSPF and #FrizzyHairProduct show that people are increasingly seeking functional, protective solutions — prioritising formulas that address real-world conditions like sun exposure and humidity, with a preference for efficacy and daily utility. In a recent development, on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags highlight a consumer focus on specialised education, age-specific needs and event-driven beauty goals. In the skincare space, sensory experiences, targeted treatments and barrier-conscious hydration are among consumer trends. It has been revealed that on TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reflect an interest in bold self-expression, approachable learning and real-talk beauty concerns.Hashtags such as #RedBlushMakeup and #CardiBNails show a clear appetite for statement looks inspired by pop culture and celebrities, where colour and confidence take centre stage. #BeginnerBrows and #BodyWaveHairstyles point to a desire for accessible tutorials and entry-level techniques, as users look for easy ways to level up their routines with minimal intimidation. Industry observers note that haircare consumers are increasingly focused on scalp and root health, as seen through the rise of scalp serums and pre-shampoo treatments focusing on preventative and foundational care. Consumers are increasingly turning to science-backed and dermatologist-associated brands like Arey, Cerave, and Vichy, signalling a desire for clinically validated solutions for scalp and hair health. Meanwhile, the growth of TGIN highlights demand for textured hair-focused, inclusive brands that cater to diverse needs with plant-based formulations. Dove Men’s rise underscores the expanding male grooming and selfcare market, whereby men are seeking straightforward yet specialised products. Altogether, these trends show a broader shift towards personalised, health-oriented and inclusive haircare solutions that balance efficacy with accessibility.

According to recent reports, in the burgeoning wellness space, there is a growing emphasis on emotional balance, stress management and functional optimisation. According to recent reports, on beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reveal a consumer desire for long-lasting performance, culturally rooted wisdom and product validation through community discovery. It has been revealed that in the TikTok space, consumer mindsets are centring around practicality, inclusivity and education in beauty routines. #AcnecareRoutine and #3StepSkincare highlight a growing demand for straightforward, step-based regimes, especially those that are accessible and targeted towards specific skin concerns like acne.
