💡 Key Takeaways
  • Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love.
  • Sources indicate that I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most important beard care product, just after beard trimmers.
  • Recent findings suggest that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So, you've realized. Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love. Thankfully, the best beard oil will keep that sculpted scruff feeling great! And not just for you, either, because the right beard oil leaves your skin glowing—and stops your facial hair from annoying any partner who gets close to it. Great beard oils also keep coarse hair from getting brittle and wiry, and soften your beard so you’re not scratching your neck or dealing with beard dandruff (yes, it exists). All that from just a couple drops of wonder oil.

Sources indicate that I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most important beard care product, just after beard trimmers. And it’s a close second. Because whether you keep your facial hair at a precise 24-hour stubble, go full hermit-mode, or stay somewhere in between, a beard oil does irreplaceable work. (The kind you can’t replace with any old moisturizer or conditioner.) So, if you’re tired of flyaways, coarse beard hair, dandruff, or itchiness, these GQ-tested and approved beard oils will turn your scruff into fluff. Promise.

Recent findings suggest that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer. (At the time of writing, we’re talking nearly 30,000 reviews and a 4.5-star rating.) And often, I'll intentionally seek out an alternative to these Amazon-beloved grooming products—if only because it feels like the equivalent of recommending Applebee's to an out-of-towner. But this time, well: Welcome to Applebee's.

In a recent development, frankly, I couldn't find a better beard oil. Not only is Honest Amish cost-effective (at the second-best price-per-ounce on my list), but the brand nailed the blend. It's a pure oil recipe (no non-oil ingredients), with seven carrier oils and seven essential oils that give it an earthy scent and help tone the skin beneath your bushel. It absorbs fast, works great to smooth down flyaways, relax stiff bristles, and battle both dry skin and flake-prone beards. And did I mention the value? Six bucks per ounce is a steal.

Industry observers note that to be clear, I only use Honest Amish on my beard, largely because I'm not a fan of using any essential oils on bare skin—I particularly find that pumpkin seed oil (a key ingredient here) can be slightly pore-clogging on acne-prone skin. That stated: I count myself as acne-prone and haven't had challenges with Honest Amish, so I'm probably being over-cautious. It's really just that good.

Despite the name Beardbrand, this company's product line covers the whole body, with a focus on multi-tasking grooming products like dual washes, all-purpose balms, and this utilitarian oil. You'll catch me using it on my hands, elbows, and hair—whether for a dash of shine (to offset a matte hair product) or a protective coat against frizz and humidity. But Beardbrand's Utility Oil is on this list because it works beautifully in the beard.

Sure, it's a touch heavier than some other oils—but that also makes it a terrific pre-shave lubricant. It's key to note that no matter which “flavor” you choose, this oil has a strong dash of fragrance. They're all good, but I'm partial to the brand's fresh Bold Fortune scent, which oozes a sexy combo of leather, oud, and tobacco. (And pro-tip: The brand's utility wash has the same come-hither scent, if you want to double down.).

Recent findings suggest that horace's beard oil will make a lot of you happy, though for different reasons. For those overwhelmed by scents—particularly artificial ones—you'll appreciate that its got the subtlest of aromas. I'm partial to the Lemon & Mint one, which reads as “fresh" and never overwhelms. For those looking to stay away from chemicals, Horace's formula is 99% natural—and the 1% is a synthetic grapeseed oil, not something with 12 syllables, which I'm fine with.

Recent findings suggest that the brand gets bonus marks for its easily-understood ingredients labels, which break down these details and err on the side of much-appreciated transparency. Finally, if you're on the fence about beard oils, Horace will make you a believer. It absorbs fast, gives a pinch of shine, and makes just enough difference in terms of taming, moisturizing, and softening that you'll see why a beard oil makes sense.

In the grooming world, Jack Black (the brand) has earned its own fanbase, thanks in large part to one product—the signature Jack Black beard oil. Apply just a few drops and it immediately goes to work softening coarse and brittle facial hair, and without an overpowering fragrance that will distract you all day long. It's one of the most popular beard oils on Amazon, but don't hold that against it. While it softens and adds shine, this oil also delivers a dose of antioxidants and vitamins from natural ingredients such as brown algae and rosemary.

According to recent reports, it also uses a unique blend of oils with the subtlest whiff of melon fragrance. Instead of the usual suspects (jojoba, avocado, sunflower seed), this product uses Kalahari melon oil, marula oil, and plum oil, which moisturize your facial hair and skin on contact. Because these oils are all fast-absorbing (my beard hair soaks it up like a sponge), they make this product much less greasy than other beard oils, giving it a more premium feel.

I test literally hundreds of grooming products a year, and I'm so intimately acquainted with brands latest and old that I often think about them based on their best product. For Pura d'Or, it's this organic beard oil. It's the best value on this list, at $3 per fluid ounce. Given how promptly you can go through beard oil—just think, if you're applying up to twice a day, that dollar-per-ounce math becomes vital. So, in addition to being my budget pick, this also gets my recommendation as the best beard oil for substantial beards.

It has been revealed that of course, it's only key if the formula measures up—and here, it does. There are two carrier oils, argan and jojoba, along with a bit of grapefruit peel and some sandalwood essential oil for both a natural scent and a touch of antimicrobial powers. It's a great beard oil for anyone, no matter how big your bank account, but if you're bearding on a budget, you'll appreciate how much goodness Pura d'Or packs into a few bucks.

Blind Barber's tonka-tinged oil is wonderful for the guy who wants to moisturize skin and whiskers with the same product. It wears extremely light—so much so that my oily skin barely registers its presence—and I find its carrier-oil-centric and shea-butter-forward formula especially comforting on the skin. It should be noted that this formula includes artificial perfume, so fragrance-averse individuals should steer clear. But for those of us who want a special scent, a flake-free beard, and soothed skin, Blind Barber's beard oil does it all.

While I'd use most of the above options as both a hair oil and a beard oil, Aesop's is one where I think of it as a hair oil first and foremost. It brings control without making things look greasy, while trapping moisture and stopping frizz. I'll use it in short hair to tame down the sides, in medium lengths (mixed with a cream or clay) for added shine, or in long hair to prevent split ends. Then, once my hair's settled up, I'll run my hands through my beard afterward. So, if you want a great hair oil with beard benefits, Aesop's is the winner.

Since the beginning of the men's grooming boom, I've been waiting for the massive designer fashion houses to start catering to guys with facial hair. For now, Tom Ford's beard oil stands alone. So, how does the designer oil stack up against our everyday favorites? After trying it out, I can tell you it’s better as a fragrance than a beard oil, but the scent alone earns it a spot in this guide.

The tobacco vanilla fragrance is much more sophisticated than what we’re used to seeing, or smelling, in this space. The scent puts an emphasis on vanilla, and you just need one or two pumps for full coverage. Considering the price and the name on the bottle, we were shocked to find this oil comes in a plastic pump bottle, but that fragrance. If you want to buy beard oil as a gift, this premium conditioning oil is a step up over your average Amazon brand, even if it doesn't soften coarse hair as well as some of our other options.

It has been revealed that if you have sensitive skin—or if you're afraid of your beard oil clashing with your daily cologne—then Marlowe makes one of the only fragrance-free beard oils. Most beard oil formulas contain both essential oils and some type of perfume oil (or, parfum, for my fellow ingredients detectives), which can be risky for your skin, follicles, and pores, so it’s nice to have an option for acne-prone and sensitive skin types.

It has been revealed that this beard oil couldn’t be simpler—and I mean that in a good way. Marlowe No. 143 has an all-oil formula and just four ingredients: safflower seed oil, sunflower seed oil, corn oil, and soybean oil. That’s it. Considering the average beauty product contains up to a dozen ingredients we can’t even pronounce, it’s a refreshing change. Although, I have to say, if you want the softest possible beard, Honest Amish also makes a fragrance-free oil.

Most guys use beard oil to tame flyaways. But what if you want the thickest, fullest beard possible? In that case, I’d recommend reaching for Bevel’s oil. This brand makes skin and hair products for Black men, but anyone with coarse or curly hair can benefit from their products. GQ contributor Timothy Beck Werth reports that this oil gave him a thicker-looking beard without excess frizz, which isn't easy to do. (BTW, that’s as much as you can expect from any beard oil, so please don’t fall for the “beard growth serums” you’ll find all over the internet.).

Industry observers note that for parched facial hair, the grapeseed, macadamia, jojoba, and argan oil will condition your beard and add a healthy shine. For beneath the scruff, the avocado and primrose oil with soothe your skin without clogging up your pores and follicles. Werth says this beard oil instantly softened his facial hair, and he also liked the sweeter smell of the macadamia-based formula. Most beard oils opt for woodsy fragrances, and the more subtle scent profile here is a nice surprise, he explains.

According to recent reports, anthony’s conditioning beard oil is a 2-in-1 product—a pre-shave oil and regular beard oil. That approach can be risky, since a lot of multipurpose products try to be everything and succeed at nothing, but luckily that’s not the case here. If you regularly cycle between clean-shaven, stubble, and full-on lighthouse keeper, then you can still use this product daily. As a pre-shave oil, it moisturizes the skin and softens facial hair for a smoother shave with fewer morning-after red bumps. As a beard oil, it hydrates, then locks in that moisture so your beard stays soft and shiny all day. I found the consistency to be somewhere in between a leave-in conditioner gel and a traditional oil, making it thicker and less messy to apply.

Sources indicate that the oil also has an herbaceous, minty fragrance that’s so refreshing it feels like aromatherapy every time you run it through your hair. That’s because the formula is full of ingredients that smell good, feel good, and actually help your skin and hair. It uses carrier oils like soybean and castor to deliver skin-pleasing and antimicrobial botanicals such as rosemary, basil, tea tree oil, eucalyptus, and spearmint. And on the hydration front, calendula and olive oil nourish your whiskers into their softest, fluffiest selves. Because of the more complex fragrance and ingredients profile, this wouldn’t be my pick for guys with sensitive skin. Still, it’s a multi-functional serum you’ll look forward to using every day.

Lots of beard oils promise to get flyaways under control, yet those rogue hairs keep popping up. So, what do you do? Instead of trying yet another oil, try reaching for a product that’s more of a leave-in conditioner for your beard. We’ve previously praised Zeus’s beard brushes, but the California-based brand also makes a beard serum that deserves a spot in your bathroom cabinet. I love that this beard oil has the simplest possible ingredients list: sweet almond oil, soybean oil, argan seed oil, trihydroxystearin, avocado oil, and fragrance.

The only multi-syllable ingredient there is a simple thickening agent, which gives this refined beard oil a gel-like consistency. That thicker formula will also put flyaways in their place. The very subtle fragrance is more Mediterranean than winter pine forest (we tested the Verbena Lime version), but you can also opt for a fragrance-free formula if you have sensitive skin or allergies. The plastic bottle uses an air pump, letting you get every last drop of oil. For clean freaks who hate the messiness and spillage that always comes with beard oil application, this is another bonus.

Tired of being left out of couple’s skincare night just because those stupid sheet masks won’t hold onto your glorious beard? Cardon’s got you, boo. Actually, this bead oil hack is perfect for guys who only sparingly use beard oil on an as-needed basis.

Sources indicate that the bamboo and charcoal sheet mask is specially shaped for guys with beards, and each mask comes with a dose of beard oil made with argan and jojoba oil. In the Venn diagram of Korean skincare and beard care products, this sheet mask-beard oil duo is the tiny, microscopic bit of overlap in the middle.

The best best oil should support your skin and your beard, and Baxter of California's sweet-smelling oil doesn't sacrifice one for the other. In his guide to the best beard care products, GQ's Timothy Beck Werth said that “In our testing, no beard oil absorbs as quickly or spreads as evenly as this one.” Squalane helps nourish the most overlooked skin on your face, while avocado oil, vitamin E, and botanical extracts smooth out your beard.

As with anything you put on your skin, the ingredients are what matter most. And with beard oils, there are two categories of ingredients: carrier oils and essential oils. No two ingredients will perform exactly the same. Some will help with very specific situations or conditions; some may actively aggravate your skin. Essential oils in particular can aggravate skin if used by themselves. So, consider the following carrier oils and essential oils, favored both by myself and Alyssa Bachowski, a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg, NYC barbershop.

According to recent reports, carrier oils—often vegetable and see oils—make up the bulk of these beard oil formulas, bringing beard nourishment and skin hydration. The most popular carrier oils are argan oil and jojoba oil (both of which Bachowski recommends), though there are dozens of varieties, from castor to marula to grape seed oils. They're usually unscented, though some—like coconut oil—may carry an aroma. Because carrier oils make up the “base” of the oil, they should be among the first to appear in a product's formula or list of ingredients.

It has been revealed that “Jojoba oil is non-comedogenic, which means it will not clog your pores. It is also a lighter oil that is absorbent, so it won't just sit on top of the hair and give you a greasy appearance,” Bachowski notes. Along with argan oil, you’re going to see a lot of jojoba oil in most popular beard oil blends.

According to recent reports, “Argan oil is filled with a ton of vitamins and minerals, as well as linoleic acid, sterolins, and squalene. All of these aid in protecting and keeping your skin and beard healthy,” Bachowski says.

“Castor oil is known for promoting beard hair growth,” indicates Bachowski. It’s hypothetically the best beard-growth oil of the crew, because it acts like a vitamin for your strands—though there's more on that below in the FAQs. But don't expect it to grow more hairs, or thicker hairs. Castor oil does have a smoke-and-mirrors benefit, at least. “It is a heavier oil and dark in color, so it can give the appearance of a denser beard on men with dark facial hair,” Bachowski says.

Grape seed oil can help tone down your skin's oil production, and is extremely moisturizing for scruff and skin alike.

Rich in fatty acids, this is a frontrunner for “most nourishing oil” for your skin and whiskers.

Yes, shea butter is in fact a carrier oil, and it has supremely moisturizing properties that make it great for detangling scraggly beards and softening stiff hairs.

It has been revealed that essential oils are distillations from more potent sources, and they tend to be additive—and active—ingredients in a beard oil. These oils are typically extracted through steaming methods, and their range of benefits can include antimicrobial properties, oil-toning abilities, and soothing superpowers. Typically, any natural fragrance in a beard oil will come from essential oils. But pure essential oils can be extremely damaging to the skin.

“You should not apply pure essential oil to a beard—it will do the opposite of what you are trying to achieve,” Bachowski says. “These [pure oils] are not good for your beard nor your skin. as they can be irritating and harmful. Essential oils can cause dryness, itchiness, and redness—and some people may have allergic reactions to them.” This is exactly why you want beard oils from trusted, tested brand.

Bachowski likes cedarwood oil for its naturally astringent properties. “It helps cleanse the pores and prevent ingrown hairs,” she adds. It also adds a natural fragrance.

“Sandalwood has anti-inflammatory properties that help reduce any skin irritation,” Bachowski says of this deliciously scented oil.

Lavender helps calm inflammation and redness, says Bachowski. Plus it brings lavender's soothing scent.

This antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, oil-toning ingredient is terrific for acne-prone faces and oily skin types.

Along with its refreshing scent, grapefruit peel oil helps nourish and detangle.

As GQ's lead grooming product reviewer, I've tried just about every beard oil in the biz. The ones chosen for this roundup excel at protecting and moisturizing both skin and hair, with minimal risk for things like inverse reactions and blemishes. They absorb cleanly, unless they expressly choose not to (like those which expressly use silicone), and they smell terrific (with both natural and artificially scented options). I've tested beard oils for a decade, on a beard that's been long, short, and everything in between. I've also scoured online reviews to confirm that these products are backed by throngs of loyal fans, whose collective opinion echoes my own experiences.

What is the best beard oil according to GQ?

With more than a decade of testing beard oils under his belt, GQ’s expert tester chose Honest Amish as the best beard oil. And 29,000 Amazon shoppers have rated this same product 4.5 out of 5 stars.

What is the difference between beard balm vs. oil?

Both beard balm and beard oil are both terrific for facial hair—but they don't do the same job. Beard balm is optimal for taming and styling facial hair, especially at medium and longer lengths. Beard oil provides less control over the shape and style, but is excellent at softening and conditioning the hairs and the skin underneath (preventing beard itch, beard dandruff, and split ends).

Sources indicate that after using a beard wash, most beard oils are applied the same way: “Start off with 2-3 drops in the palm of your hand,” says Bachowski. “Rub it into your hands so that it is evenly distributed from fingertips to the heel of your hand. Start by rubbing the oil with your fingertips onto the skin beneath the beard hair, then eventually working the oil from root to tip of the actual beard. Make sure to also apply oil to your neck and cheeks where you may have shaved or trimmed as well. If you feel like the 2-3 drops wasn't enough based on the length or density of your beard, apply another 2-3 drops.”.

How do you prevent beard dandruff?

Industry observers note that preventing beard dandruff starts with changing your skincare regimen. Namely, introducing exfoliation and moisturizing products that can get past a thick nest of facial hair. For exfoliation, look for physical scrubs (even a beard brush will work). For the best moisturizing effects, be sure to apply beard oil both morning and night. The beard oil will also soften and condition the facial hair to prevent itchiness.

Does beard oil help grow a beard?

It has been revealed that no, beard oil is not meant to help beard hair growth, whether that’s to make facial hair thicker or grow faster. To be honest, we don’t know of much that can really change your scruff's density besides a beard transplant and maybe minoxidil. Beard oil is here to make your existing beard hair softer and more cooperative, while also nourishing the skin beneath the beard—skin that’s often prone to dehydration and dandruff. It’s already doing a lot.

Recent findings suggest that absolutely. Beard oil is a great investment for anyone with facial hair, since it can help soften and tame your scruff while simultaneously moisturizing the skin underneath. This means no more itching, no flyaways, and no beard dandruff.

Alyssa Bachowski is a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg NYC barbershop location.

‘Political malpractice’: Calls grow to delay Senate GOP leadership elections

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1087 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., walks through the Ohio Clock Corridor this summer.
  • After last week’s midterm elections saw them lose at least seven Senate seats and the majority, some Republicans are pushing for a reckoning, saying the conference should stop and think about its future.
  • “After the stunning defeat [we] just can’t continue on business as usual.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., walks through the Ohio Clock Corridor this summer. Now he’s pushing to delay leadership elections for his conference, urging a discussion of last week’s larger than expected losses. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

After last week’s midterm elections saw them lose at least seven Senate seats and the majority, some Republicans are pushing for a reckoning, saying the conference should stop and think about its future.

“After the stunning defeat [we] just can’t continue on business as usual. That kind of defeat demands change,” Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said on Monday evening.

According to recent reports, asked if he himself would want to run for Senate minority leader, the Wisconsin Republican responded with a question of his own: “That’s part of our problem. Who’d want the job? Would you want it?”.

Sources indicate that though no hopeful had emerged as of Monday afternoon — at least publicly — to challenge current Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., for the top GOP post, the frustration was palpable as Republican senators returned to D.C. and grappled with the election results. Calls grew throughout the day to delay the conference’s leadership elections planned for Tuesday morning.

According to recent reports, “Well, I mean, I’m open to hearing what the arguments are for that,” Thune told reporters Monday when asked about the possibility of postponing the leadership votes. “I don’t know if that solves anything, but like I said, it’s going to be a decision that’s ultimately made by Republican senators. We’ll hear them out.”.

Recent findings suggest that johnson told reporters on Monday that if the election is held, he would “leave the room” and walk out. Either way, he seemed certain to at least get a “fulsome” discussion of the topic, as he requested in a letter he sent to Republican Conference Chair Tom Cotton, R-Ark. Four other Republican senators signed on to the letter, hitting the threshold to call a conference meeting under internal GOP rules.

According to recent reports, also signed by Sens. Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, Rick Scott of Florida, and John Kennedy of Louisiana, the letter obtained by CQ Roll Call cites last week’s “stunning defeat” and reads in part: “Holding leadership elections without engaging in a robust discussion and evaluation of how those running for leadership intend to lead would be political malpractice.”.

Kennedy noted Monday evening that he was asking to postpone the leadership elections because “we need time to talk to each other.”.

Industry observers note that “We’re like a shop owner who’s losing his customers. It’s not the customer’s job to fix that. It’s the shop owner’s job, and I’m not looking for blame-shifting. I’m looking for self-examination,” he remarked, adding that he wouldn’t consider running for minority leader himself.

In the letter, the group asked that at the time the leadership elections were set to begin, 9 a.m. on Tuesday, they instead “have a fulsome conference discussion and delay holding leadership elections until we all have a chance to hear from leadership candidates as to what type of collaborative conference governing model we should adopt and what our strategy will be to counter the emboldened Democrats.”.

Thune echoed that wording Monday as he spoke to reporters, saying, “I do think that we need to have a very fulsome, robust conversation about where we go from here, and then we’ll see what the consensus of the conference is.”.

Recent findings suggest that but Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., who serves as chair of the Senate Republican Policy Committee, said she has seen such requests introduced in the past and didn’t think it would do much to affect the ultimate outcome. “I think Sen. Thune will be reelected,” she said.

In a recent development, and several Senate GOP aides stated that they suspected a “robust” conversation wouldn’t do much to delay the plans and that leadership elections were still expected to take place Tuesday. They noted similar efforts from some of those same senators in previous years to sow discord in the ranks.

In a recent development, that includes Scott, who unsuccessfully challenged Thune in 2024 and then-GOP leader Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., in 2022. But Scott told Fox News over the weekend, “I don’t want to run again. I’ve run twice.”.

Republicans “failed. We had a horrible night,” Scott mentioned. “Instead of having an [leadership] election, the first thing you do is you say, ‘OK, what are we going to change? We have to change something.’”.

Lee floated the idea of waiting until after the uncalled Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska are officially resolved.

An online pressure campaign was building in some of the same MAGA corners of the internet that have pushed to pass a sweeping voter ID bill, known as the SAVE America Act, that has stalled in the Senate. On Monday morning, influencer Scott Presler in an X post urged constituents to call their senators while praising the lawmakers who have already pushed for the leadership elections to be postponed. “Where is everyone else?” he wrote.

Sens. Jim Banks of Indiana and Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania also called for a delay, though they did not appear on Johnson’s letter.

According to recent reports, “A week ago, we had the worst election results in decades,” McCormick noted in a post on X, calling Tuesday “too soon” to vote for leaders. “I know it’s been practice to go straight to leadership elections in recent years, but we should not rush it.”.

Banks similarly said Tuesday was “too soon,” posting on social media, “Our conference needs to sit down and have a frank conversation about where we fell short, what we stand for, and what we’re going to do for the working families who sent us here.”.

One senator speaking out in Thune’s defense was Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who competed with Thune for the top spot in 2024 but on Monday noted the leader isn’t to blame for the midterm results.

“I think the president needs to look in the mirror and look at the flawed candidates that he endorsed, and the kind of environment that we’re in,” remarked Cornyn, who is still smarting from losing his primary to a challenger backed by President Donald Trump.

In a recent development, cornyn’s loss means he has no say in the coming conference leadership elections. But he noted, “I think Thune’s a good man, and did as well as he could against a president and an environment that was pretty hostile.”.

Latest Update: Lafayette 148’s Emily Smith on 30 Years in Fashion and Finding Her Uniform

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between.
  • I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher.
  • It has been revealed that I was a bagger at Kroger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between. This month, we sat down with Lafayette 148 creative director Emily Smith as the New York-based fashion house celebrates its 30th anniversary. Smith has spent more than two decades at the helm of the brand, working her way up from a part-time freelancer to creative lead. But her fashion ambitions began long before she arrived in New York. Growing up in Atlanta, she ran her own neighborhood art camp before discovering designers like Donna Karan and realizing fashion could be a career. Now, Smith is celebrating the women who have shaped Lafayette 148 through its “Uniform” campaign, which highlights accomplished New Yorkers and their individual approaches to personal style. Below, Smith reflects on her unconventional start, why she’s stayed at the organization for over 20 years, and the career advice she wishes she’d followed sooner.

I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher. It was basically babysitting all the neighborhood kids, but I created a flyer, got paid for it, and did the whole thing. I started in second grade, and we did it every year for about eight years. I even started hiring people so we could have two classes going at once. We had swimming lessons. The local news even came and did a segment on it. I loved decorating my classroom and setting everything up. My parents were so nice to give me the garage and basement to do it all. Not necessarily an official job, but my first money-making moment.

It has been revealed that I was a bagger at Kroger. It just was not for me.

I was always creative growing up. At a certain point, I discovered Donna Karan. It’s kind of crazy when you see somebody doing something and suddenly realize, Oh, that’s a career. I can do that. I became obsessed with everything in the ’90s, all the Newly introduced York fashion at the time. That was when I decided I wanted to pursue it. When college applications came around, my mom really encouraged me to go to art school. I started in fashion, and that became my focus. Growing up in Atlanta, I wasn’t necessarily surrounded by a major fashion community. But my dad’s office was across the street from the art museum at one point, and I remember going there and having that exposure. My mom was always crafty and creative, too. She really encouraged us to be who we were.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a language creative people have that’s a little different from the way business people communicate. When I went to art school, I felt like I’d found my people. It wasn’t just fashion people. It was photographers, fine artists, and all these different kinds of creatives. Being around people who thought about things differently was really inspiring. Even today, I thrive around people who have creative insight. There’s always a little more depth to the way they see things.

I interned at Bill Blass for about six months. I moved to Latest York in July 2001, and we had our fashion show on September 10. I remember Marc Jacobs had his show that day, too, and everybody was celebrating. People were saying, “Just come a little late to work tomorrow.” And then, obviously, September 11 happened. A week later, the entire team was let go, from the top down. What I learned from that experience was the fragility of everything. Don’t take anything for granted. Anything can come and go in a moment. But I also worked with Lars Nilsson and Hervé Pierre Braillard, who were just the kindest people. This industry has a little bit of everything, but I loved that they led with kindness, even when they were under so much pressure. As an intern, I was literally carrying ironing boards down the street and doing a sketch here or there. It was very much about doing whatever needed to be done.

After my internship, I had a brief stint of freelancing. Those were some long months. I remember coming home from one job and my roommates asking how my day was. I mentioned, “Well, I was putting pigs on socks.” I knew I wouldn’t be going back. Freelancing is hard. It’s a grind, but you meet a lot of great people. I actually made some really good contacts during that time. I eventually met Deirdre [Quinn], Lafayette 148’s founder. She met with me on a Saturday, which I thought was incredible. I was really just looking for advice. I wasn’t looking for a job, and I didn’t even know much about the brand. It was only five years old. She was so kind, full of knowledge, and passionate. After I spent a year freelancing and meeting people who seemed so over the industry, her enthusiasm reminded me why I wanted to do this in the first place. She offered me a part-time freelance position, and the rest is history.

In the beginning, security was really important to me. The idea of losing a job and having to pay rent was scary, so that was definitely part of it initially. But really, it was the growth. Within a couple of years, they were sending me to the factory. It was a small, tight-knit company, so I was able to wear a lot of different hats. I had a mentor named Barbara Gast who was traveling back and forth from Italy, and I was learning so much from her. I’d compare notes with friends in the industry and realize how much hands-on experience I was getting. I understood the value of that and really loved being so close to the product. It never got boring. And whenever things did get slightly boring, I’d ask, “Okay, what’s next?” And there was always something. It’s such an entrepreneurial place that you can almost create your next opportunity. That’s what made it so exciting.

I think if you asked Deirdre, she’d have a different answer because she has her own experience of building the firm. For me, it’s about having started at a company that was really a factory and being part of the journey of building its identity and what it stands for. I was the kid running up and down the factory floors collecting samples. That hustle and bustle was so innate to who the brand was. To me, it was really exciting to build more of a brand story around that. Thirty years later, we’re still celebrating those roots and making sure we haven’t strayed too far from them, while continuing to evolve. Being part of that journey has been really exciting.

The constant has always been this idea of an accomplished woman. She’s always been at the forefront of who we’re designing for. At the time, it was the career woman. But now, what does that even mean anymore? What does that look like? There are so many different versions of that woman and so many different ways people dress. At the heart of it, she’s a woman who knows what she wants. She’s busy and has a really full life, whether she’s starting her career or ending it. They can all find something in the clothes.

Sources indicate that for us, it was about choosing people who inspire us. Number one, they had to be New York women. That was the base. We wanted women who make us want to be better ourselves. From someone like Deborah Berke, the architect, to women who have built incredible careers in other fields, it’s important to shine a light on them. I think back to when I was a kid and how much you need that kind of inspiration. Even at a certain stage in your career, when you’re wondering what the point is, it’s nice to have people who inspire you. These are women who have really built something for themselves, and I think that’s worth celebrating.

According to recent reports, sophie de Rakoff noted something during the project that I really liked, and I’m going to steal it: “Dressing with intention.” When you know yourself, you know what works on you. It’s no longer about dressing to impress. There’s a confidence in knowing what works for you and making it work. We’re all so busy. Who has time to overthink getting dressed? You know what works, and you build a system around that. You’re able to create a wardrobe that really works for you. Everybody has a different definition of a uniform, and that was the whole point of the project.

When I first started in the industry, I was a total hippie. I was making my own clothes, and they were terrible. Absolutely falling apart. It was what it was. I think part of the change comes from not having as much time as you did when you were younger. But it’s also about simplicity and comfort. I know that if I’m going to be on the floor pinning something but also have to give a presentation, there are certain pieces that work for both. I can be comfortable and still feel appropriately dressed. I’ve found a handful of things that work for me, and I don’t have to think too much about them anymore. A crisp, oversize white cotton button-down is half my closet. I also love a soft skirt and a major chunky sweater. Those are the pieces I always go back to and interchange depending on the day. I even wear sweaters in the summer. It’s cold in the Navy Yard!

Our pants fit incredibly well. The moment somebody gets into our pants, they’ll love us forever. Then it’s the jacket and the white shirt. Those three things are our gateway pieces, and everything else follows. You need a good blazer and a good leather piece, too. Once you find those foundational pieces that really work for you, everything else becomes easier.

In a recent development, I really want to see more women in our clothes. It’s not just about growing the business. It makes me happy when I see people put on our clothes and feel really good. We work so hard to make sure things fit the way a woman wants them to fit. I just want more people to enjoy that.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Miley Cyrus can buy herself flowers, but we have a feeling that her beau, Maxx Morando, is buying them for her.

Recent findings suggest that since 2021, the Disney Channel alum has been linked to Morando, a fellow musician who is perhaps best known as being the drummer for the rock band Liily. He was also previously part of another group, called the Regrettes. In 2022, Lilly was invited to play on Cyrus’s TV special, Miley’s Latest Year’s Eve Party.

Sources indicate that throughout their years-long relationship, the two have preferred to keep their romance largely out of the spotlight. But Cyrus offered a rare glimpse into their life together during her interview for the Harper’s Bazaar’s December 2024/January 2025 cover story. “He’s very similar to me,” she said. “We just don’t take life too seriously.”.

Throughout their time together, they’ve also collaborated numerous times in the studio, with Morando serving as a producer and songwriter on Cyrus’s Something Beautiful and Bass Persuades records. In her interview with Bazaar, Cyrus revealed that music was actually how she and Morando first got to know each other. “I’ve always worked with the people that I love,” Cyrus said. “And Maxx just inspires me so much.”.

Now, the pair are engaged and reported to be getting married this weekend with an intimate ceremony in Southern California. However, other details are being kept under wraps—for now.

It has been revealed that if you’re wondering what else there is to know about Cyrus and Morando’s low-key romance, then look no further. Below, we’ve tracked the couple’s entire relationship from start to finish.

For Cyrus, it was love at first sight, but for Morando, he already had an idea of who he was meeting long before the date even happened.

“We got put on a blind date,” Cyrus reveals in an interview with British Vogue years after the fact, in May 2023. “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him. I thought, ‘The worst that can happen is I leave.’ ”.

According to recent reports, when he calls mid-interview, her phone starts playing “Tyrone” by Erykah Badu. “I call that ‘boyfriend sexy ringtone,’ ” she claims, smiling.

In an interview with Vogue, Cyrus discusses the outfits that she wore for her sets at Summerfest in Milwaukee and Atlanta’s Music Midtown festival. Turns out, one of the pieces—a faux-leather set crafted by Shane Kastl—includes cartoon monsters sketched by Morando.

During the interview, Cyrus comments on the custom design, saying, “This look is a one-of-a-kind collaboration between two of my favorite emerging artists, Maxx Morando and Shane Kastl. Shane used existing pieces I’ve collected over time and customized Maxx’s cartoon characters [within] his construction. Their collaboration is the perfect example of sustainability becoming the next fashion phase, and it proves that anything can be reinvented, which resonates with me deeply.”.

The pair spark dating rumors when they make their first public appearance at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show in November.

Industry observers note that for the event, Cyrus wears a metallic blue fringe dress with a contrasting cream feather drop waist, which she pairs with strappy golden sandals. Meanwhile, Morando sports a burgundy suit over a G-logo top, with white sneakers featuring the signature Gucci red and green stripes.

According to recent reports, shortly after the event, Cyrus shares a slideshow where the third photo sees her and Morando posing together on the red carpet. In her caption, the singer writes, “LOVE PARADE ❤️💕 @gucci @alessandro_michele.”.

Recent findings suggest that A fan captures a sweet video of Morando supporting Cyrus backstage for her NBC holiday special, Miley’s Newly introduced Year’s Eve Party. In the clip, the two can be seen smiling and dancing together.

Days later, paparazzi snap photos of the two enjoying a vacation together in Miami, where the special was filmed.

Cyrus and Morando make a rare joint appearance together for Versace’s Fall/Winter 2023 fashion show in West Hollywood.

Later in the day, the two attend the launch party for Cyrus’s eighth studio album, Endless Summer Vacation, in Beverly Hills. Paparazzi photos—which you can see here—show Cyrus dressed to the nines in a sparkly black one-shoulder minidress and a vibrant green fur jacket. Morando looks equally stylish in a navy-blue velvet suit.

A source tells People where Cyrus’s head is at amid her relationship with Morando.

Recent findings suggest that “She’s the healthiest and happiest she’s been in a long time,” the source says, then goes on to describe how Cyrus has healed following her 2020 divorce from Liam Hemsworth: “Everyone was blaming her for the divorce and calling her this wild child, but that wasn’t fair. Their relationship and marriage was toxic, and she was heartbroken.”.

A second insider tells the outlet that Morando is a “cool guy.”.

In a recent development, “He has no interest in being a huge celebrity; he’s very low-key. Miley loves these qualities,” the source explains. “Miley can be herself. They are supportive of each other’s careers. Miley is enjoying life and things are great.”.

Morando supports Cyrus at the 66th-annual Grammy Awards ceremony, where the singer wins her first-ever golden gramophone.

During the ceremony, the couple is joined by Cyrus’s family members, mom Tish Cyrus and sister Brandi Cyrus.

A source for People opens up about Cyrus and Morando’s joyful home life together.

“She is very happy with him,” the insider claims. “Miley has changed a lot in the past couple of years. She seems more calm and harmonious. Everyone loves Maxx. He’s a great guy. She is very happy with him. He’s private and doesn’t like being in the press. It’s been good for her.”.

In a upcoming Dolce & Gabbana campaign video, Cyrus poses in a sultry all-black look and shares the song “Imitate,” a track from Morando’s band, Liily.

Cyrus offers rare details on her love story with Morando in an interview for Bazaar’s December 2024/January 2025 cover story.

It has been revealed that “He’s very similar to me. We just don’t take life too seriously,” she says.

While the two have a small age gap—Cyrus is six years Morando’s senior—she reflects on how their different upbringings have made them approach life differently.

“He looks at life really differently than I do,” she explains. “He grew up with a laptop. I had a desktop computer that I shared with my brothers and sisters. … Honestly, he’s raised our dog off Reddit. I’m like, Are you sure we’re supposed to be doing this? And he’s like, On Reddit it claims blah, blah, blah.”.

She also opens up about working with Morando on musical projects and how collaboration is her love language. “I worked with my dad forever. That’s how me and my ex-husband met each other. I’ve always worked with the people that I love,” Cyrus notes. “And Maxx just inspires me so much.”.

Morando and Cyrus are photographed behind-the-scenes at the 67th Grammy Awards, where Cyrus snags her third Grammy for her collaboration on Beyoncé’s “II Most Wanted.” The appearance marks a rare joint public outing by the couple, who match in all-black ensembles.

Morando wears his usual red-carpet uniform to stand by his partner at the 97th Academy Awards. Cyrus wears a black gown with a distressed bodice embellished with sequins, which she wears with a curly hairdo and bleached brows.

Cyrus and Morando walk the red carpet for the Hollywood premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash, and there, the singer debuts a chunky gold ring with a large, square diamond at the center.

Hours later, People confirms the two are engaged.

The engaged pair wear cool all-black looks to the show and look so in love as they embrace at their star-studded table during the ceremony.

Cyrus is sleek in a moto-inspired fit from Celine, while Morando goes low-key in a black T-shirt and pants.

Following their engagement news, a source tells People that the couple wants a “smaller and meaningful” wedding rather than a “huge, traditional” event.

“Maxx is extremely private, and that’s just not who he is,” the source says. “When they do get married, it will be something smaller and meaningful to them. Not a major Hollywood production.”.

Recent findings suggest that while it’s unclear when the Hannah Montana singer plans to wed her drummer fiancé, the source notes Cyrus is enjoying this era and her engagement: “Miley really loves her life right now. Everything just feels like it’s falling into place for her.”.

At the world premiere of the Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special in Los Angeles, Cyrus walks the red carpet alongside her fiancé.

For the occasion, the Disney Channel alum wears a plunging silver Rabanne dress layered over a bedazzled Hannah Montana tee, while her beau opts for a white tee and black jeans, which he pairs with black-and-white sneakers from Celine.

Cyrus is honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, thanks to her “lasting impact on the entertainment industry.” In reference to Cyrus’s work on Hannah Montana and more, Walk of Fame producer Ana Martinez notes: “Generations of young girls have grown up watching her evolve, finding inspiration in her journey and fearless creativity.”.

At the ceremony, Cyrus is supported by members of her family like mom Tish and her older half-sister, Brandi. Meanwhile, Morando shows his support too, posing with Cyrus in front of the plaque.

Nearly a year after the pair reveal their engagement, TMZ reports that they will tie the knot with a secret ceremony in Southern California, scheduled to take place on the weekend of November 20.

Although other details are kept under wraps, Cyrus is seen running errands—like like getting her nails done—ahead of the ceremony.

She seemed to have been teasing the nuptials a month prior, when she brought out Morando during her Hollywood Bowl shows to do a surprise rendition of “Let’s Get Married.”.

  • “Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting.
  • Opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when Terence Young, the director of Dr. No, needed a suit for Sean Connery to wear for his debut as James Bond, he took him to see his personal Savile Row tailor, Anthony Sinclair.

“Connery’s suits were considered relatively contemporary, because Anthony always had a very soft shoulder on his suits,” explains Elliot Mason, the director of business at Anthony Sinclair, which is no longer located on Savile Row, but still makes classic British suiting. “Anthony liked to nip in the waist, so it gave that real hourglass silhouette to the suit, which really is quite timeless. And as was the trend at the time, the Connery suits all had a relatively high rise, double-pleated with English forward pleats, and most of his trousers had Daks button-tab adjusters on the side.”.

Opting to dress James Bond in a Savile Row suit might seem like a no-brainer in hindsight, but the decision—and the cut of the suits themselves—still resonates more than 60 years later. Sinclair would make all of Connery’s suits during his nine-year run as James Bond, and his blend of classic British tailoring and of-the-moment influences would create a template for every Bond to come. With Robert Pattinson—a Dior ambassador and a guy with a reputation for adventurous style—chosen to take up the mantle in Bond 26, the question now becomes: what will he wear?

Tailor Anthony Sinclair fitting Sean Connery for one of the suits he wore in 1963’s From Russia With Love.

Ian Fleming, the author who created James Bond, spent a lot of time talking about what Agent 007 drank (Wolfschmidt Vodka) what he drove (Bentley convertibles, for the most part) and how he made his coffee (he was a dedicated pour-over guy), but, surprisingly, he never specified where the spy bought his clothes. As a result, for the last six decades, it’s been up to the directors and costume designers of the 25 previous films to create a newly introduced look for every successive Bond. In the Connery and Moore eras it was Savile Row suits. Timothy Dalton’s Bond wore Paul Smith. Brosnan was a bespoke Brioni guy, as was Daniel Craig, who also brought Tom Ford into the mix. At 6’1” to Craig’s 5’10”, with a leaner build, and a long track record of fashion-forward dressing, Pattinson has everything needed to reinvent Bond once again.

According to recent reports, “I’m pretty sure we’re going to see something quite different from Pattinson's Bond,” says Matt Spaiser, the tailoring obsessive behind BondSuits.com and the author of From Tailors with Love: An Evolution of Menswear Through the Bond Films. “Pattinson is a different kind of actor, and he’s going to wear something that moves differently. Plus, he’s 18 years younger than Daniel Craig.”.

Sources indicate that the actor playing Bond has a major influence on how he dresses—Daniel Craig, an adventurous dresser himself, was very hands-on with the wardrobe in his films—but Pattinson’s ongoing contract with Dior could also factor in. “Some of his Dior looks look somewhat like James Bond—he wears a great tuxedo—but I don’t think it’s going to tell us what he’s going to wear as James Bond,” Spaiser says. “He’s worn suits from other brands in other roles—like in Tenet, he wasn’t wearing a Dior suit—so I don’t think he's necessarily obligated to be wearing Dior as James Bond.”.

Daniel Craig, seen here in 2019 with then-Prince Charles on the set of No Time to Die, mainly sported sharp Tom Ford suiting in his later Bond films.

Another important factor that contributes to a upcoming Bond’s look is what’s happening in fashion whenever the film eventually gets made. “One thing that we've seen throughout most of the Bond eras is that he dresses in suits that are fairly traditional, but there's always some nod to the era that they’re in,” indicates Spaiser. “Sometimes they lean a little more into fashion, like when Roger Moore was wearing flares. That was something that I think they couldn't avoid without making Bond look too old-fashioned at the time.”.

According to recent reports, tone also plays an vital role, and historically has ping-ponged between serious (Connery, Dalton, Craig) and more campy (Moore, Brosnan), but with Denis Villeneuve, the auteur behind Sicario, Blade Runner: 2049, and Dune in the director’s chair, the smart money isn’t on hovercraft gondolas and punny Bond girl names. A darker, more atmospheric milieu could make for an interesting complement to Pattinson’s taste for high-fashion.

Industry observers note that if Mason were dressing Pattinson for the role, he states, he’d take a lead from his clientele, many of whom, like Bond, are well-heeled Londoners with a taste for expensive sports cars and well mixed cocktails. “The majority of our customers are reasonably conservative, and when it comes to fit, they’re sensitive to current trends,” Mason notes. As such, he’d opt for longer jackets, both single- and double-breasted, that are fuller through the body, and straight-leg pleated trousers. “It’s not that very, very slim fit that we'd seen for so many years, but it still needs to be refined,” he says. “I don’t think it would be appropriate to put him in wide-leg or baggy trousers. I just don't think it’s right for Bond.”.

Robert Pattinson, the latest 007, has been the face of Dior’s menswear for over a decade.

Sources indicate that given the intense scrutiny on every relaunch of the Bond franchise, and the tendency of fans to get worked up online over perceived mishandling of a beloved character, Pattinson, Villeneuve, and the film’s yet-to-be-announced costume designers have little room for error. Go too conservative and they’ll be accused of playing it safe; make Bond into a fashion guy, and they’ll incur the wrath of the traditionalists.

“He needs to look current, but also timeless,” Spaiser claims. “It’s a hard balance to find.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Capitol Dome is illuminated before dawn on Oct. 13. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

OPINION — Once again, the next Congress is going to be filled with losers.

This is not a personal judgment about their character or personality, but a simple recognition that many members have lost races before getting elected. And the incoming class is no different.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve written many versions of this column for more than a decade, and yet the lesson always seems to get lost, no pun intended. Parties routinely attack candidates who enter a race with losses on their record. And, of course, it happened this cycle as well.

“We beat him once. We’ll beat him again,” National Republican Senatorial Committee Chairman Tim Scott declared when Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown confirmed his challenge to appointed GOP Sen. Jon Husted in the summer of 2025.

“Ohioans gladly sent him packing last year, and they’ll not hesitate to toss him aside again,” stated a Republican strategist.

Recent findings suggest that brown lost reelection to Republican Bernie Moreno in 2024 but came back to defeat Husted for the state’s other Senate seat. And Brown is far from the only candidate to avenge a loss with an electoral victory last week.

According to recent reports, the fact of the matter is that losing a race doesn’t have to be the end of a political career. Losses can lay the foundation for future success by building name ID or a fundraising network. Or sometimes it takes a change in the political environment or change in circumstances, such as running for an open seat instead of challenging an incumbent.

In addition to Brown, there are more than a dozen losers coming into the next Congress:.

In some instances, though, the losses are piling up.

Republican Rep. John James of Michigan now has three statewide losses on his record. He lost Senate contests in 2018 (taking 46 percent of the vote) and 2020 (48 percent) and came up short in his bid for governor this year (44 percent).

It has been revealed that republican former Sen. John E. Sununu of Latest Hampshire, who lost reelection in 2008 to Democrat Jeanne Shaheen, fell in his comeback attempt for the open seat last week.

But they could take heart from another repeat loser. Charlie Crist, a former Florida governor and congressman, has had a handful of high-profile losses over the years, including for Senate and two gubernatorial comeback bids. He was just elected mayor of St. Petersburg.

So even though I know it’s a futile request, let’s have a bipartisan agreement not to attack candidates for past losses, because losing doesn’t mean they can’t later pull off a win.

And as online chatter about plastic surgery—who did it, and what did they do—reaches a fever pitch, Lawrence is setting the record straight by openly discussing her “upcoming” breast implants.

During an appearance on Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen, alongside her Hunger Games co-star Josh Hutcherson, Lawrence told Cohen offhandedly that she “has implants.” When Cohen asked, she stated they’re new and credited Santa Monica–based plastic surgeon Steven Teitelbaum.

Lawrence went on to say she went with a full-C implant, restoring her breasts to the “same size they were”—meaning, before she had two kids. This is the second time in recent months that the Oscar winner has admitted to a postpartum plastic surgery procedure. In an interview with The Cut for her new haircare brand, Mes, Lawrence admitted to getting a breast lift following the birth of her second child. “Everything bounced back, pretty much, after the first one,” the actress told The New Yorker in October 2025. “Second one, nothing bounced back.”.

She took that sentiment even further on an October 2026 episode of Call Her Daddy, where she gave host Alex Cooper, who was then pregnant, a frank piece of motherly wisdom: “Your vagina will bounce back, your butthole won’t.”.

Lawrence is the latest in a string of A-list celebrities opening up about cosmetic treatments, like Kylie Jenner, who made waves last year when she admitted on TikTok to her exact implant size and surgeon. From Lawrence, the casual admission feels less like a calculated confession and more like advice from a trusted friend who doesn’t hold back about motherhood and pregnancy’s physical toll.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here at Harper’s Bazaar, we are game to try anything and everything in the wellness world—from daily digestion walks to a $500 full-body assessment, and even supplements to boost ferritin levels—to stay healthy. But, like anyone else, we’re always hunting for new ways to avoid getting sick.

According to recent reports, we’ve all been there: someone coughing on the subway immediately makes you jump, or you hear a friend you just sat next to at dinner has come down with a cold, and suddenly you’re overdosing on vitamin C. Warding off a cold or viral sickness is not always possible—especially once cold and flu season rolls around.

In a recent development, there are classic tricks like upping your vitamin C intake, washing your hands frequently, and drinking hot liquids like soup and tea, but what about the extreme hacks that hit the SOS button on your immune system—those under-the-radar, witchcraft-adjacent tricks? We have tried almost every tip and trick in the book—some work like a charm, and others are all hype and anecdotes—but ahead are the 14 hacks our editors swear by for staying healthy this cold season—and beyond.

In a recent development, “Tongue scraping has changed my life. Not only does it make your mouth feel much cleaner and support overall oral health, but I swear that since I started scraping religiously a few years back, I've been sick WAY less often. And I have a toddler! In daycare! My theory is that it scrapes away bacteria before it has a chance to settle in your throat—but who knows? No matter what the science notes, there are only upsides—fresher breath, better teeth, and the satisfaction of seeing all that gunk removed." —Jenna Rosenstein, beauty director.

“As an out-and-proud hypochondriac, I have a long laundry list of cold-fighting hacks. The most crucial is washing my hands frequently (as soon as I arrive somewhere fresh, after taking the subway, after touching a public surface, etc.) and avoiding touching my face. I keep a compact hand sanitizer in every purse I own in case of emergency!” — Olivia Alchek, senior designer.

Sources indicate that “I consider a good night's sleep a cure-all for just about anything, including incoming sickness. Not only does adequate rest help your body fight off infection by way of antibody and immune cell production, but it just makes you feel better in general, which is all you want when you're feeling borderline sick.” —Tiffany Dodson Davis, beauty commerce editor.

“Most of my heavy-hitting cold fighters are from Europe (they’re just exponentially better over there), but when it comes to sick solutions stateside, I always have Wellness Formula stocked in my house. I don’t know what sorcery is in these pills, but once I take this, whether it’s when a sniffle or tickle in my throat comes up, or if I am already deep into a cold, I feel better the next day. The pills contain all the gold-standard immunity ingredients: elderberry, zinc, propolis, echinacea, and vitamins C and D, plus vitamins and minerals that are good to take generally, like selenium, calcium, and vitamin A. The only downside is a pungent aftertaste (likely from the garlic bulb in the formula), and the daily dose is 6 pills, which is more than many can handle. If you don’t like pills, there’s a liquid version that works just as well, but I prefer the pills for when I travel.” —Katie Intner, beauty market and commerce editor.

“Even in the post-COVID era, I still wear K-N95 masks on public transit. It’s the most successful way to avoid unwanted germs. Thinking about thousands of New Yorkers on a crowded subway, sniffling in the winter months—I’ll never go back to being mask-free again!” —OA.

In a recent development, “As soon as I feel a scratchy throat coming on, I break out the Vicks. Slather it on and let it do its old-timey magic.” —Lillian Dondero, assistant managing editor.

It has been revealed that “When people say to ‘flush out a cold,’ they typically mean drink lots of fluids, but I love dry brushing to get the lymphatic system moving and grooving to rid any toxins from the cold. I do it for two minutes before I shower, and I instantly feel my lymphatic system activated and more energized. Plus, it doubles as exfoliation, which is key during the winter months.” —KI.

“Throat Coat tea is my holy grail whenever I’m feeling under the weather. I love the subtle licorice flavor, and it’s incredibly soothing on an irritated throat. I always keep it stocked at home and reach for it at the first sign of a cold. Honestly, it’s so good that I even drink it when I’m not sick!” —Jackie Judd, executive assistant.

“Whenever the thought ‘Oh, I think I might be getting a cold’ enters my brain, I immediately go to the pharmacy to pick up some Zicam. I don’t know if this is the official tagline, but in my head it is ‘stops a cold before you get it’ because IT. DOES! The trick is to buy the kind that goes up your nose—spray or swabs—and be diligent; your symptoms won't progress, and then they'll go away completely. It's magic!” —Laia Garcia-Furtado, deputy culture director.

“A shot before work is my way of staying healthy! My fridge is always stocked with Greenhouse Juice Co. dispensers because I truly can never live without them. A quick shot to kickstart my day is a great immunity boost, and the spice is a great bonus, as it always helps wake me up.” —Claudia Cruz, deputy visual director.

“Liquid echinacea everywhere! I keep it in my bag and squeeze it into everything—even my coffee.” —Lynette Nylander, executive digital director.

“I love Cymbiotika’s liposomal technology because the lipid base makes it more easily absorbed into the bloodstream and is therefore more effective. I always use these vitamin C packets when I feel a cold coming on or know I will be low on sleep, like while traveling, because they truly boost my immunity and taste like a creamsicle. Life is hard enough! I want a supplement that works and tastes good.

I will often couple the Cymbiotika vitamin C with a packet of the Armra Colostrum, which protects and boosts immunity.” —KI.

“When I’m already experiencing cold symptoms? Downing a spoonful of honey—both anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial—with a squeeze of lemon does wonders for my itchy throat or stubborn cough." —TDD.

“My most homeopathic tip whenever I start to feel symptoms is to eat raw garlic. Garlic contains a compound called allicin, which is released when you crush, chop, or chew it. Allicin is known to have immune-boosting, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties that may shorten illness. Does it actually work? Who knows! But it doesn’t hurt to crush a little garlic in olive oil for dipping toast. It’s a harmless, delicious extra step in my sick day routine.” —OA.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

Recent findings suggest that I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he stated he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Industry observers note that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

In a recent development, mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

According to recent reports, set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

According to recent reports, transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

Bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Industry observers note that do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The area where I grew up, Belleville, is really different from the Hamptons,” said Casablanca’s Charaf Tajer. “Growing up between Paris and Morocco, it seemed a very different landscape: it sounded very exotic to me.” Globalization might have shrunk the world—and flattened it too—but distance still creates room for the imagination to generate glamour. For this resort season Tajer projected his Casablanca formula on the Hamptons.

His starting point was a survey of Jackie Kennedy and the milieu of American East Coast society during the middle of the last century. The seaside estates, sailing boats, country clubs, and sprawling lawns of this privileged playground offered a new destination for a brand whose MO has always been rooted in a romanticized dislocation. “It’s kind of near the cities,” Tajer said of the Hamptons, “but it has its own bubble.” Peering into that bubble through documentaries and archival imagery was an exercise in escapism, and Tajer intended this collection to be an escape route too. “It’s not that I don’t care: I’m really into the news. But I also feel like we need to care less, because the news can take us into a mental spiral.”.

According to recent reports, tajer presented the collection as the wardrobe of a dynastic clan on vacation, with each member bringing their own interpretation of American sportswear through a Casablanca-fied lens. Although shot in the UK, closer to Hertfordshire than the Hamptons, the images were cleverly set and staged. A scion crunched the gravel with a chunky laborador in a nicely homaged embroidered Skyliner jacket, wearing wide-leg chinos in one shot and skate shorts in another. Another lounged on a plump couch in seasonally-printed tennis gear, or lurked on the stairs in a camp collar shirt and embroidered wide-leg pants.

Industry observers note that the women wore striped knitted separates, scarf-print silks, and tennis dresses, as well as a long black knitted dress that offered a more universal option for evening. Throughout, the preppy and streetwear references were blended and sometimes distorted through color, proportion, and the prints and embroidered illustrations created by the brand’s three in-house artists.

According to recent reports, the chinoiserie pattern adapted from a stately temple jar in this synthetic Camelot backdrop was prominently transposed into prints and patches. For Tajer, it served both as a hint toward a future project and as a reminder of how the decorative vernacular of one culture can become the status symbols of another.

Tajer said his ambition is to create a Casablanca wardrobe that can accommodate almost any occasion. The silk shirts that established the label have been joined by much more: This season’s additions included a leather tracksuit and new hybrid driving/boat shoe. Tajer cited Ralph Lauren as an inspiration, saying: “This is always what I wanted to create with Casablanca: a full, cohesive world.”.
